chapter_name: Chapter 02: The Sentence Structure and Clauses
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will understand the difference between phrases and clauses, and learn to identify and construct Simple, Compound, and Complex sentences.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Sentences are like trains! Some have just one main engine (Simple), some link two engines together (Compound), and some have an engine pulling extra passenger cars (Complex). Let's become sentence engineers! 🚂

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A Phrase is a group of words that makes some sense but lacks a subject and a verb (e.g., 'in the morning'). A Clause is a group of words that MUST have a Subject and a Verb. Clauses are the building blocks of full sentences.
examples_or_templates: Clause: the monster hid under the bed (Subject = monster, Verb = hid)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: An Independent (Main) Clause makes complete sense on its own. A Dependent (Subordinate) Clause has a subject and verb, but starts with a subordinating word (like because, if, when) and cannot stand alone as a full sentence.
examples_or_templates: Independent: The team won the match. (Makes perfect sense)
Dependent: ...because they practiced hard. (Leaves you asking, 'What happened because they practiced?')

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Simple = 1 Independent Clause. Compound = 2 Independent Clauses joined by a Coordinating Conjunction (FANBOYS: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So). Complex = 1 Independent Clause + 1 (or more) Dependent Clauses joined by a Subordinating Conjunction (AWUBIS: Although, When, Until, Because, If, Since).
examples_or_templates: Compound: I love pizza, BUT my brother prefers burgers.
Complex: I eat pizza WHENEVER I go to Italy.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which of the following is a Compound Sentence?
options: Although it was raining, we went outside.
The bright green frog hopped away.
I wanted to go to the park, but it started raining.
Running through the forest, the deer escaped.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: I wanted to go to the park, but it started raining.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ What type of clause is: 'If you finish your homework'?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Identify the sentence structure: 'The dog barked loudly because he saw a stranger.'
subjective_practice.hint: Look for the conjunction 'because'. Is it linking two equal engines, or is one a passenger car?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Join these two simple sentences to make a Compound sentence using a FANBOYS conjunction: 'The sun was shining. The wind was cold.'
subjective_practice.hint: These are contrasting ideas. Which conjunction means 'however'?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Identify the dependent clause in this sentence: 'Although she was tired, Maria finished reading her book.'
subjective_practice.hint: Look for the clause that starts with a subordinating conjunction and cannot stand alone.

activity_or_assignment.title: ✂️ The Clause Connector
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write 3 independent clauses on blue paper strips, and 3 dependent clauses on yellow strips. Mix and match them to create 3 completely different Complex sentences!

chapter_summary: ⭐ A phrase lacks a subject/verb; a clause always has a subject and a verb.
⭐ Independent clauses stand alone; dependent clauses rely on the main clause to make sense.
⭐ Sentences can be Simple (1 clause), Compound (2 independent), or Complex (1 independent + 1 dependent).
